newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet fuel trades lower at $24.25.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet fuel trades lower at $24.25.

text.p: The Singapore middle-distillate market remained soft on Thursday despite a 1.33-million-barrel stocks draw as traders said the supply overhang remained to haunt the market.
They said stocks for the week ended July 2 at 10.74 million barrels were still higher than the normal monthly average of six to eight million barrels, while regional demand remained scarce.

Jet fuel was traded between a US trader and a European major at $24.25 per barrel for July 18-22 lifting, free-on-board (fob) basis. This was lower than the last deal done on June 26 at $24.65 for July 11-15 lifting.

Gas oil was steady, with a major offering at $164 per tonne ($22.00 per barrel) for July 18-22 lifting fob basis, while a German trader offered at $22.00 for July 21-25. Buyers were not atrracted by such offer levels, traders said.

They said there were talk of deals done earlier this week at a 75-cent-per-barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, fob basis, and a 44,000-tonne cargo sold on an inter-tank-transfer basis at $21.75 per barrel.

India's August-March term diesel tender was seen attracting low offers of around $1.20 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, cost-and-freight basis to the Indian west coast, and around $2.20 per barrel above MidEast quotes, c-and-f east coast.
This worked out to around 35 cents per barrel fob basis.
But traders said India considered this to be too high, and were seeking to buy at between parity and 10 cents per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, fob basis.
Swaps gas oil for July shaved off 25 cents to be last quoted at $22.15/$22.25 per barrel, while August lost five cents to $22.80/$22.90.
